requirement_text.ISS-0332: REQ-077 bumped the DEFINITION_PROMOTED platform-event-type seed from schema_version 1 (review_id required non-null) to schema_version 2 (review_id nullable) in lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex. This seed only applies to newly provisioned tenants. Pre-existing tenants' event_type_registry still has v1. R10 against such a tenant commits the promotion transaction, then fails the event-append step on schema validation -- Severity-1 broken-audit shape. Needs a backfill routine.

task.description:
Validate CODE-DESIGNER's design artefact at lib/letflow/design/iss0332-definition-promoted-backfill.md (on branch feature/WF03-ISS0332-20260826). Check out that branch before reading the file.

Validation criteria:
1. Every ISS-0332 acceptance criterion is explicitly mapped to a design element (AC1: backfill updates pre-existing tenants; AC2: R10 succeeds end-to-end; AC3: idempotent on already-v2 tenants).
2. Scope decision (backfill only vs structural fix) is stated with rationale.
3. Backfill module/function name and @spec are stated -- no implementation code present.
4. All register_type/2 return value cases are addressed (ok, duplicate_event_type_version, schema_version_not_monotonic, tenant_not_provisioned, other).
5. The design is unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without making new design decisions.
6. No implementation code in the design doc (function bodies, actual Elixir code, etc.).

If PASS: complete handoff with status PASS and next_action 'ORCH routes to ELIXIR-DEV for implementation'.
If FAIL: list specific issues; ORCH will rework with CODE-DESIGNER.
acceptance_criteria: All six validation criteria checked against the actual design doc
PASS verdict only if all six criteria are met
FAIL verdict with specific issues if any criterion fails

result.next_action: ORCH routes to ELIXIR-DEV for implementation

criteria_checked.notes: Section 5 has an explicit table mapping AC1 (Backfill.run/1 iterates all tenants via Repo.all on Registration + register_type/2 per tenant), AC2 (post-backfill get_type/2 returns v2 schema admitting null review_id, so append succeeds), and AC3 (both :duplicate_event_type_version and :schema_version_not_monotonic treated as skipped no-ops, idempotent on re-run).

Section 2 gives a three-point rationale for why the structural fix (wrapping event_appender in an outer transaction) is not feasible in ISS-0332 scope: (1) event_appender is opaque/injected, (2) the step-9-outside-transaction shape is a stated architectural invariant requiring REVIEWER sign-off, (3) the gap predates ISS-0332. Decision: backfill only. Follow-on issue noted for structural gap.

criteria_checked.criterion: 3 - Module/function name and @spec stated, no implementation code
criteria_checked.notes: Module Letflow.TenantProvisioning.Backfill in lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill.ex. Public function run/1 with full @spec: event_type_attrs :: map() -> {:ok, %{updated: non_neg_integer(), skipped: non_neg_integer()}} | {:error, {:backfill_failed, tenant_id :: Ecto.UUID.t(), reason :: term()}}. No function bodies or real logic expressions present -- only specs and prose.

Registry @spec has six variants: {:ok, EventType.t()}, {:error, :tenant_not_provisioned}, {:error, Ecto.Changeset.t()}, {:error, :duplicate_event_type_version}, {:error, :schema_version_not_monotonic}, {:error, term()}. Section 4 table covers all five required categories: {ok,_} -> updated, :duplicate_event_type_version -> skipped, :schema_version_not_monotonic -> skipped, :tenant_not_provisioned -> warn+skip, {:error, other} -> halt (description explicitly names 'changeset validation failure' as an example of this catch-all, covering Ecto.Changeset.t()).

All core behaviors specified: module, file path, public function, @spec, iteration strategy (Repo.all on Registration table in public schema), per-tenant call (register_type/2 with v2 attrs and tenant_id), counter semantics (updated vs skipped), error halting logic, Mix task name and file path. The only 'ELIXIR-DEV to decide' is whether to inline the v2 attrs literal in the Mix task or expose via a public helper -- the design pre-approves BOTH paths explicitly, so no incorrect choice can be made. This is an implementation style choice between two pre-approved equivalents, not an unresolved design decision.
Design doc contains only @spec type annotations, prose descriptions, and tables. No function bodies, no pattern-match arms, no real Elixir expressions with operational logic.
